newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA'S COSTELLO URGES STATE TAX REFUND.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA'S COSTELLO URGES STATE TAX REFUND.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday that the six states must refund to industry pre-payments for illegal provincial taxes about to be replaced by the national government.
"There shouldn't be double taxation," Costello told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.

"If you have already in the kick pre-payments of liquor fees and the Commonwealth (national government) comes along to start collecting them at you request from August 5, there shouldn't be any double taxation," Costello said.
Australia's High Court last week outlawed A$5 billion of alcohol, tobacco and petrol taxes levied by the six states and two territories.
Canberra has agreed to levy the taxes on behalf of the states and return the money to them.

The states became embroiled in a row with industry over whether some of the outlawed taxes were paid in advance and how the taxes would be applied and refunds given to ensure prices remained steady. Victoria and Queensland have agreed to repay some pre-payments, but New South Wales continues to refuse.
Under the constitution, Canberra must charge the same rate in all states. But the taxes overturned by the court varied from state to state.
The national government will levy its taxes at the highest rate, with low-tax states providing refunds.
